info.title: MarketMitra API
info.description: Public + session-scoped HTTP API for the MarketMitra dashboard. For automated / agent access to public market data, prefer the MCP server at /api/mcp (see /llms.txt and docs/api-surface.md). Session-scoped endpoints authenticate via the Clerk session cookie in hosted mode; in self-host mode they resolve to a single local user with no login.

tags.name: Market data
tags.description: Public. Also available as MCP tools at /api/mcp.

tags.name: Watchlists
tags.description: Session-scoped. The user's own named stock watchlists (Markets page). Paths and stored fields keep the legacy `wishlists` name.

tags.name: AI
tags.description: Session-scoped. BYO-key AI insights + chat. 400 no_ai_key when the user has no key.

tags.name: Settings
tags.description: Session-scoped. The user's encrypted AI provider key.

cookieAuth.name: __session
cookieAuth.description: Clerk session cookie (hosted mode). Sent automatically by the browser; the API explorer uses your current session.

bearerAuth.description: Personal access token, hosted mode only. Create one in Settings > Account > API access tokens; it is shown once. A read token allows GET only, a write token allows all methods. Tokens work on the data API and are rejected on /api/settings, /api/cron, /api/advisor and /api/system/logs. Rate limited per token.

get.description: Live search across ~2,570 NSE equities + tracked indices. Proxies fundamentals-api; returns the array directly (not the standard envelope).

200.description: Up to 15 matches, index matches first.

get.description: Screener.in-style aggregate for one NSE company in a single call: company profile, a live quote (ADR 0024: yahoo-finance2, falling back to NSE/BSE), ratios, shareholding pattern, peer comparison, document links, and financial statements. Pick `sections` to narrow the response. Returns the object directly (not the standard envelope) — same deliberate exception as GET /api/search and GET /api/news. Shares its aggregation logic with the MCP `get_company_fundamentals` tool.

parameters.name: sections
parameters.description: Comma-separated subset of: company, quote, ratios, shareholding, peers, documents, financials. Omit for all.

200.description: { symbol, found: true, company?, quote?, ratios?, shareholding?, peers?, documents?, financials? } — fields present per `sections`.

404.description: { symbol, found: false, message } — not a symbol the fundamentals service recognises, or every source came up short.

get.description: Recent Indian-markets headlines. Omit `symbols` for the broad stream. `sentiment` is headline tone, not a signal. Page with `cursor` from `next_cursor`.

Filter the NSE stock universe (bulk-refreshed at most once daily from a screener_metrics table — see ADR 0025) by market cap, P/E, P/B, ROE, ROCE, dividend yield, debt/equity, and 3y sales/profit growth CAGR, plus sector/industry equality. Fixed-field min/max only — no free-form query expressions (deferred to a later phase). Excludes companies whose last scrape failed. Sorted by market cap descending unless `sort_by`/`order` are given (server-side, over the whole matching set; NULLs last). Market cap, price, P/E, P/B and dividend yield refresh daily for the whole universe; ROE, ROCE, debt/equity and growth are scraped incrementally, so those filters only match companies that have been scraped yet. Same schema Mitra's run_screener MCP tool uses. Returns the array directly (not the standard envelope). Paginate with `limit` + `offset`; the total number of matches (ignoring paging) is returned in the `X-Total-Count` response header.

400.description: A `_min`/`_max`/`limit` value wasn't a valid number.

get.description: The user's saved notes (Phase 10 / ADR 0020), newest-updated first. Notes also feed the user's private retrieval corpus.

200.description: All the user's alerts, newest first.

post.summary: Create an alert (or upsert the IPO watch)
post.description: Body is a discriminated union on `type`: price_threshold | percent_move | week52_breach | portfolio_pnl | ipo | ipo_watch. `ipo_watch` is upserted (one per user) and returns 200.

get.description: Every alert Mitra created or changed on its own — the default-guardrail hook on a new holding, or its own chat tools (ADR 0030) — most recent first, each with the reason Mitra gave. Does not include a user's own edits made directly through the Alerts page.

post.description: `{id}` marks one; `{}` or `{all:true}` marks all.

get.description: Never returns the key — only provider, model, and a last-4 hint.

put.description: Validates the key with a live call before storing it. 503 without SETTINGS_ENC_KEY on the server.

post.description: Neutral synthesis of a company's public fundamentals. Per-user cache, 24h. Requires the user's own AI key. Rate limited (ai tier).

Three items from figures computed on the server: `return` (today's net rupee and % move and the top contributor), `exposure` (largest holding / sector weight) and `risk` (active price alerts within 3% of triggering, else none). Reply `content` is JSON, `{ items: [{ key, tone, text }] }` (tone: positive | neutral | warning). Uses the caller's own AI key (BYOK). Cached per user (shared for IPOs); briefs cached before v0.4.0 were prose and are regenerated. Body `{ force? }` (`{ slug, force? }` for an IPO).

200.description: { success, data: { content: '{"items":[{"key","tone","text"}]}', model, generatedAt }, meta: { cached } }

post.description: Four items: `listing` (GMP, GMP % and the implied listing price from the price band, the GMP being an unofficial estimate), `offer` (size, lot, minimum investment, subscription, dates), `business` and `risk` (only from retrieved filings or news, otherwise stated as not available). Reply `content` is JSON, `{ items: [{ key, tone, text }] }` (tone: positive | neutral | warning). Uses the caller's own AI key (BYOK). Cached per user (shared for IPOs); briefs cached before v0.4.0 were prose and are regenerated. Body `{ force? }` (`{ slug, force? }` for an IPO).

200.description: { success, data: { content: '{"items":[{"key","tone","text"}]}', model, generatedAt }, meta: { cached } }

post.description: A longer structured brief (markdown sections: what it is / recent developments / the numbers / risks / open questions), retrieval + synthesis. Subject is one of company | theme | portfolio | comparison. Requires the user's own AI key. Not cached (ephemeral). Rate limited (ai tier).

Kicks off an async, checkpointed run over one stock: analyst team → bull/bear debate → synthesis (ADR 0021). ~15–20 LLM calls on the caller's own key over a few minutes. Returns immediately with a run id to poll. One run in flight per user. No trade decision is ever produced — the output is a debated analytical briefing.

409.description: A run is already in progress for this user.

post.summary: Advance one phase of one agent run
post.description: Machine-to-machine. Bearer CRON_SECRET (dev-open, prod-503). Claims the oldest resumable run (or `?id=`), runs one phase, persists, and re-invokes itself until done. `.github/workflows/agents-tick.yml` calls it every 5 min as a safety net for dropped self-calls.

parameters.name: id
parameters.description: Target one run instead of the sweep.

post.description: Streamed text/plain token response (not the envelope). Tool-calling loop: `search_context` over the retrieval corpus plus the read-only market-data tools. Completed turns are persisted; the user's recent questions feed their private retrieval layer. Rate limited (ai tier).

delete.description: Deletes the caller's stored chat turns and drops their 'recent questions' entry from the retrieval corpus.

post.description: The Model Context Protocol endpoint. Client config: { "url": "https://<host>/api/mcp" }. Requires header `Accept: application/json, text/event-stream`. Tools: search_symbols, get_quote, get_company_fundamentals, get_price_history, get_news, list_ipos, get_market_indices. Send `initialize`, then `tools/list` / `tools/call`. Public, rate limited (mcp tier).

200.description: A JSON-RPC result (as an SSE `message` event or JSON, per the client's Accept header).

post.description: Machine-to-machine. Bearer CRON_SECRET (dev-open, prod-503 when unset). No-ops outside NSE session hours unless ?force=1. Vercel Cron / GitHub Actions issue GET; both are accepted.

post.summary: Reflect on finished agent runs (Phase 11 Part C)
post.description: Machine-to-machine. Bearer CRON_SECRET (dev-open, prod-503). For each `done` multi-agent run older than the reflection horizon (~21 days) with no reflection, writes a hindsight 'lessons' note comparing the debate's key claims to the stock's actual move, and prunes runs older than 120 days. `.github/workflows/agents-reflect.yml` calls it daily. Lessons are per-user and feed future runs.

200.description: { considered, written, skipped, error, pruned, errors }

post.description: Machine-to-machine (Phase 10 / ADR 0020). Bearer CRON_SECRET (dev-open, prod-503 when unset). Pulls recent news, chunks + embeds it locally, upserts into the `chunks` collection with userId=null, prunes stale news. GET and POST both accepted. `?indexesOnly=1` just ensures the collection + Atlas Vector Search indexes and returns.

parameters.name: indexesOnly
parameters.description: Ensure indexes only; do not index.

parameters.name: newsLimit
parameters.description: How many recent news items to (re)consider (default 150).

200.description: { vectorIndex, news: { seen, changed, pruned }, errors, ms }

post.summary: Extract proposed portfolio holdings from an uploaded file (ADR 0022)
post.description: Upload a broker screenshot (image), XLSX/CSV export, DOCX, or PDF statement. CSV/XLSX are parsed deterministically (no AI call); image/PDF/DOCX go through the caller's own AI key via structured output. Matches each extracted holding against the company database and diffs against the caller's existing holdings. Writes nothing — returns a proposed change list for the caller to review and separately approve via POST /api/portfolio-import/confirm.

Writes the user's explicitly approved subset of a POST /api/portfolio-import/extract response — the only route that actually creates/updates holdings from a Mitra-driven import. No AI involvement; a plain create-or-update per item. Never called automatically — reached only by an explicit approve action in the UI.

get.description: The user's watchlists, oldest-created first.

post.description: The name `Holdings` (any casing) is reserved for the list derived from the portfolio and returns 422.

patch.description: The name `Holdings` (any casing) is reserved for the list derived from the portfolio and returns 422.

post.summary: Add a stock to a watchlist
post.description: Adds an NSE symbol (deduped, capped at 50 per watchlist).

409.description: Watchlist not found, or already at the 50-symbol cap.

delete.summary: Remove a stock from a watchlist

get.description: Whether the user has Slack/Telegram/WhatsApp/a custom webhook connected (ADR 0028) — never returns the stored secrets themselves.

put.description: Partial update — an included field sets/replaces that channel, an included empty string clears it, an omitted field is left untouched. Values are encrypted at rest (same as the BYO AI key).

503.description: No SETTINGS_ENC_KEY configured on this deployment.

post.summary: Send a test notification on one channel
post.description: Sends a real test notification through one already-saved channel. Channel `email` sends a real test email through the same route an alert takes (the user's email setting, the server's provider and the account address); it answers 409 with the reason when email cannot be sent.

200.description: Delivery result for that one channel.

get.description: Whether adding a holding automatically creates a default trailing-stop + cumulative-drawdown alert pair for it (ADR 0030). Defaults to true.

put.summary: Turn auto-guardrail alerts on or off
put.description: Controls whether newly added holdings get a default trailing-stop + cumulative-drawdown alert pair (ADR 0030). Does not touch alerts already created.

get.description: Public. Checks MongoDB, the fundamentals API, the MCP tool registry, the Upstash rate limiter, and Clerk auth configuration in real time (no persisted history), plus the most recent event-log entry per cron job. Backs both the public /status page and the admin /system page.
Session-scoped (signed-in users only). Reads the systemEvents collection (30-day TTL), currently populated by the 3 cron routes (evaluate-alerts, index-corpus, agents-reflect).

parameters.name: before
parameters.description: Only events strictly before this ISO timestamp (pagination cursor).

post.summary: Refresh the screener's price-derived fields for the whole NSE universe
post.description: Machine-to-machine (ADR 0033). Bearer CRON_SECRET (dev-open, prod-503 when unset). Quotes every main-board NSE symbol from Yahoo in 100-symbol chunks and posts market cap (₹ Cr), price, P/E, P/B and dividend yield to fundamentals-api POST /screener/quotes (needs SCREENER_INGEST_TOKEN). GET and POST both accepted.

get.description: Sectors and industries present in the screener data, with company counts. Pass `sector` to narrow `industries` to that sector. Public, read-only.

200.description: { sectors: string[], industries: string[], sector_counts: {name: n}, industry_counts: {name: n} }

get.description: Same filter and sort parameters as GET /api/screener; `limit`/`offset` are ignored and EVERY matching row is exported (capped at 5,000). Returns text/csv with a Content-Disposition attachment filename. Text cells that start with = + - @ are prefixed with an apostrophe to defuse spreadsheet formula injection.
Whether the current disclaimer version has been accepted. Local-only: returns 404 unless ADVISOR_MODE=enabled on a non-hosted deployment.

post.description: Records acceptance of the current disclaimer version. Local-only: returns 404 unless ADVISOR_MODE=enabled on a non-hosted deployment.

get.description: The saved policy (null if none). `?format=file` downloads it as JSON. Local-only: returns 404 unless ADVISOR_MODE=enabled on a non-hosted deployment.

403.description: The Advisor disclaimer has not been accepted.

put.description: Validates (allocation sums to 100, index weights sum to 100, position limits can fill the satellite sleeve) and saves. Local-only: returns 404 unless ADVISOR_MODE=enabled on a non-hosted deployment.

403.description: The Advisor disclaimer has not been accepted.

get.description: Deterministic monthly plan from the policy: identical input gives identical output, and 'No action this month' is a valid result. Recommend-only; nothing is executed. Local-only: returns 404 unless ADVISOR_MODE=enabled on a non-hosted deployment.

403.description: The Advisor disclaimer has not been accepted.

get.description: Runs the deterministic quality screen (5-year ROCE, debt/equity, free cash flow, growth consistency, promoter pledge and trend, P/E vs own history, data freshness/completeness) and returns every gate with its measured value. A gate that cannot be evaluated is `unknown` and blocks eligibility. Local-only: 404 unless ADVISOR_MODE=enabled on a non-hosted deployment.

get.summary: Latest stored research memo for a symbol
get.description: Returns the most recent cited memo (null if none). Local-only: 404 unless ADVISOR_MODE=enabled on a non-hosted deployment.

post.description: Reads the latest annual report and the quality-screen facts, asks the user's configured model for a structured memo (business, moat, management, capital allocation, risks, thesis, kill criteria), and verifies every claim: each needs a verbatim quote from a supplied source or an explicit 'not found in provided material', and every figure must appear in a cited quote. A memo that fails verification after one repair attempt is rejected (422) and not stored. Stocks that fail the screen are refused (409) unless allowIneligible is true. Analysis only — never a trade recommendation.

filingUrl.description: Optional https URL of a filing PDF to use instead of the annual report on file.

filingText.description: Optional filing text (500–2,000,000 chars) to use instead of fetching a PDF.

409.description: Stock does not clear the screen.

422.description: Invalid input, or the memo could not be grounded.

get.description: Recorded recommendations, newest first. Local-only: 404 unless ADVISOR_MODE=enabled on a non-hosted deployment.

post.description: Records a stock (from a stored memo, with its price and kill criteria) or this month's plan. Recording is not executing. Local-only: 404 unless ADVISOR_MODE=enabled on a non-hosted deployment.

404.description: Advisor not enabled, or memo not found.

patch.description: Marks an entry followed, ignored or modified (with the amount actually invested). Local-only: 404 unless ADVISOR_MODE=enabled on a non-hosted deployment.

post.description: Evaluates every monitored recommendation's kill criteria against fresh data and notifies once per criterion that has fired. Local-only: 404 unless ADVISOR_MODE=enabled on a non-hosted deployment.

get.description: Runs the kill-criteria review for all journal entries. Not registered in vercel.json or any workflow; call it from your own scheduler with the CRON_SECRET bearer. Local-only: 404 unless ADVISOR_MODE=enabled on a non-hosted deployment.

post.description: Runs the kill-criteria review for all journal entries. Not registered in vercel.json or any workflow; call it from your own scheduler with the CRON_SECRET bearer. Local-only: 404 unless ADVISOR_MODE=enabled on a non-hosted deployment.

get.description: Paper-trades every recorded stock recommendation at that day's close against the same rupees in NIFTYBEES: per-entry results, totals (annualised only after a year), month-by-month history including losing stretches, and a plain-language warning when the stock sleeve trails the index over entries at least 180 days old. Forward tracking only — no backtest. Local-only: 404 unless ADVISOR_MODE=enabled on a non-hosted deployment.
Newest first. `q` filters by title. On a user's first visit the old single widget thread is migrated into a first conversation "Earlier chat".

delete.description: Deletes every conversation with its messages and stored attachments.

get.summary: Get a conversation and its messages
get.description: Returns the conversation and its stored AI SDK UI messages (text, file and tool parts), oldest first.

delete.description: Deletes the conversation, its messages and its stored attachments.

post.summary: Send a message to a conversation (streamed)
post.description: Server-authoritative history: send only the new user message. Attachments are references (`/api/mitra/files/{id}`) returned by the upload endpoint and must belong to the caller and this conversation. Streams the AI SDK UI-message format (SSE), runs the investing-focused agentic loop (same read-only tool allow-list and guardrail as the widget), and persists both turns. Long conversations are windowed, with older turns folded into a stored summary. Rate limited (ai tier).

200.description: An AI SDK UI message stream.

422.description: Invalid message, a missing/foreign attachment, or attachment_unsupported (e.g. audio on a Claude key).

post.description: multipart/form-data with `file` and `conversationId`. Allowed: images (PNG/JPEG/GIF/WebP), PDF, audio (MP3/WAV/OGG/FLAC/M4A/WebM) and .txt/.csv/.md. The type is decided from the file's bytes, not its name. Max 4 MB per file, 50 MB per user.

201.description: Stored. Envelope with { id, url, filename, mediaType, kind, size }.

get.description: Owner-only. Supports `Range` requests (206) so audio can seek. Served with nosniff and a sandbox CSP.

delete.description: Only for files not yet part of a sent message.

404.description: Not found, not owned, or already attached.

get.description: Chat, display and shortcut preferences. Always complete (defaults fill anything unset).

patch.description: Send any subset; unknown fields are rejected so typos are not silently dropped.

get.description: Holdings, notes, alerts, watchlists, Mitra conversations (attachments by reference only) and preferences, as one versioned JSON file. API keys and notification secrets are never included.
Daily OHLCV bars, oldest first, for one NSE ticker. Public. 502 `price_history_unavailable` means the data source failed (retry); an empty `bars` array means it answered with no rows.

200.description: Envelope with { symbol, period, bars: [{ time, open, high, low, close, volume }] }.

get.description: Operator-only. Whether outgoing email can reach real users: API key, sender address, domains verified in the provider, with plain-language issues. Read-only.

200.description: Envelope with { status: ok|warning|error, summary, sender, senderDomain, verifiedDomains, issues[] }.

post.summary: Send a test email to yourself (admin)
post.description: Operator-only. Sends one designed email (by sample id) or all of them to the caller's own address, subject prefixed [TEST]. Returns the provider's own error text per email. Rate limited per admin.

id.description: A sample id (welcome, alert-stoploss, alert-drawdown, alert-target, digest, mitra-summary, whats-new, promo, verify-email, password-reset) or "all".

200.description: Envelope with { to (masked), results: [{ id, label, ok, error? }] }; success is false if any failed.

get.description: NIFTY 50 breadth (advances / declines / unchanged over the constituents that reported; null when fewer than 25 priced) and NSE sectoral index moves, best first. Live Yahoo Finance data, cached about a minute. Breadth covers NIFTY 50 only, not the whole exchange. FII/DII flows are not offered: there is no free permitted source.

200.description: { success, data: { breadth, sectors, asOf } }. Fields are null / empty when the data source is down.

post.description: Three items: `breadth` (advances vs declines), `leaders` (strongest and weakest sector with % moves) and `catalyst` (the main headline theme). Index levels are not repeated and no institutional-flow data exists. Reply `content` is JSON, `{ items: [{ key, tone, text }] }` (tone: positive | neutral | warning). Uses the caller's own AI key (BYOK). Cached per user (shared for IPOs); briefs cached before v0.4.0 were prose and are regenerated. Body `{ force? }` (`{ slug, force? }` for an IPO).

200.description: { success, data: { content: '{"items":[{"key","tone","text"}]}', model, generatedAt }, meta: { cached } }

post.description: Three themes: `earnings`, `macro` and `sector`, each with a tone (positive / neutral = developing / warning = negative). `[TICKER]` tags appear only for tickers present in the headlines. Reply `content` is JSON, `{ items: [{ key, tone, text }] }` (tone: positive | neutral | warning). Uses the caller's own AI key (BYOK). Cached per user (shared for IPOs); briefs cached before v0.4.0 were prose and are regenerated. Body `{ force? }` (`{ slug, force? }` for an IPO).

200.description: { success, data: { content: '{"items":[{"key","tone","text"}]}', model, generatedAt }, meta: { cached } }

get.description: The signed-in user's first name (hosted accounts) and holdings with live prices, used to personalise the Mitra chat greeting and starter prompts. Own data only. Never fails because of missing quotes: unpriced holdings have a null ltp.

Whether a triggered alert is also emailed (on by default), whether an email can actually be sent right now (and why not: `disabled`, `provider_missing`, `no_address`), the masked destination address, a plain-words `blockedText` with how to fix it for this deployment, and the outcome of the last attempt.

200.description: { success, data: { enabled, deliverable, blockedBy, blockedText, maskedTo, last } }

put.summary: Turn alert emails on or off
put.description: Body `{ enabled }`. Returns the same status object as GET.

post.description: Tests the signed-in user's stored AI provider key with a tiny request and returns the provider, model and the measured round-trip latency in milliseconds. The key is never part of the response. Uses a few tokens of the user's own key. Rate limited (ai tier).

400.description: The provider rejected the key; `error` carries the reason.

get.description: The product version (SemVer, one version for the app and this API) and the short commit id the running build was made from. Public. `npm run deploy:prod` checks this after each deploy.
Deprecated: use `/api/watchlists`. Same behaviour; kept so existing clients keep working. The user's watchlists, oldest-created first.

post.description: Deprecated: use `/api/watchlists`. Same behaviour; kept so existing clients keep working.

patch.description: Deprecated: use `/api/watchlists/{id}`. Same behaviour; kept so existing clients keep working.

delete.description: Deprecated: use `/api/watchlists/{id}`. Same behaviour; kept so existing clients keep working.

post.summary: Add a stock to a watchlist (deprecated alias)
post.description: Deprecated: use `/api/watchlists/{id}/symbols`. Same behaviour; kept so existing clients keep working. Adds an NSE symbol (deduped, capped at 50 per watchlist).

409.description: Watchlist not found, or already at the 50-symbol cap.

delete.summary: Remove a stock from a watchlist (deprecated alias)
delete.description: Deprecated: use `/api/watchlists/{id}/symbols/{symbol}`. Same behaviour; kept so existing clients keep working.

get.description: Browser session only (a token cannot list tokens). Never returns a token or its hash. In self-host mode returns `enabled: false`.

200.description: { success, data: { enabled, tokens: [{ id, name, scope, prefix, createdAt, expiresAt, lastUsedAt, status }] } }

prefix.description: First characters of the token, to recognise it. Not secret.

post.description: Browser session only. Body `{ name, scope: read|write, expiry?: never|30d|90d|365d }` (default 90d). The plaintext `token` is returned once, here, and never again; only its SHA-256 hash is stored. At most 10 active tokens per user. Hosted mode only.

201.description: { success, data: { token, id, name, scope, prefix, createdAt, expiresAt, lastUsedAt, status } }. Copy `token` now.

400.description: Self-host mode: tokens are not used.

delete.description: Browser session only. Takes effect immediately.

404.description: Not found / not yours / already revoked.

post.description: Up to five points (quality, growth, valuation, ownership, risk), each with a signal (strength / neutral / concern) and text citing numbers computed from the stock's own data, written with the caller's own AI key (BYOK; hosted never uses the operator's key). Cached for 12 hours per user, symbol and mode. Mode is guarded by default (no verdicts). On a local / self-host instance a user can opt in to unrestricted mode (Settings > AI & Models), and the response may then also carry `valuation` and `entry`; the hosted site is always guarded (ADR 0054). Body `{ symbol, force? }`.

200.description: { success, data: { brief: { points: [{ key, signal, text }], valuation?, entry? }, mode: 'guarded'|'unrestricted', generatedAt }, meta: { cached } }

get.description: The Analyst Desk roster (ADR 0058): one analyst per holding, plus any watchers. Each has a status, the last check, the newest journal entry and whether its dossier is built. Also returns `auto` (the master switch for automatic analysts) and today's AI-call usage against the daily cap. Browser session only, because these endpoints control unattended use of your own AI key.

200.description: { success, data: { auto, usage: { used, cap }, analysts: [{ symbol, source, status, statusNote, hasDossier, summary, lastCheckedAt, latest }] } }

post.description: Assigns an analyst to a stock that is not a holding. Body `{ symbol }`. The dossier is built by the scheduled worker. At most 40 analysts per user.

get.summary: Read an analyst's dossier and journal
get.description: The baseline dossier (summary, business, three strengths, up to two vulnerabilities, what was not available) and the journal, newest first. Browser session only.

200.description: { success, data: { symbol, source, status, statusNote, dossier, lastCheckedAt, journal: [{ id, ts, kind, title, body, impact, alert }] } }

patch.description: Body `{ status: "active" | "paused" }`. Resuming an analyst that never built its dossier returns it to `initializing`.

delete.summary: Remove an analyst and its journal

200.description: { considered, written, skipped, error, pruned, errors }

post.description: Analyst Desk worker (ADR 0058): gives every holding an analyst, builds pending dossiers and runs the end-of-day check for analysts that are due. Bounded per run; AI is only called for a new dossier or a material event, under a per-user daily cap. Bearer `CRON_SECRET`.
